ticketTapperDefectFound.summary: server/controllers/smokecraftTicketTapperSpecialsController.js's entire write path (createSpecial, updateSpecial, trackTap, trackAdd, endSpecial, submitForApproval, approveSpecial, rejectSpecial, publishSpecial) referenced columns that do not exist anywhere in the real ticket_tapper_specials / ticket_tapper_special_events / ticket_tapper_inventory schema (migrations 017/071) — e.g. inventory_json, pricing_json, media_json, cta_json, created_by_json, approval_json, `source`, `action`, `table_label`, `guest_session_id`, `event_timestamp`, `quantity_available` on a column that is actually a GENERATED column.
ticketTapperDefectFound.howDiscovered: The connection-state health check only runs a read-only SELECT 1 ... LIMIT 1 (correctly reports CONNECTED — the table is reachable), which never exercises any write path. A real POST to /api/smokecraft/ticket-tapper/specials returned ok:true with localPreview:true and message 'Special created locally (approved) — backend unavailable', which is indistinguishable from success to any caller — the actual INSERT was throwing and being silently swallowed by a try/catch that falls through to a fake-success response.
ticketTapperDefectFound.severity: High — every real staff action in this module (create/update/approve/reject/publish a special, track a tap/add) was completely non-functional against the real database while reporting success.
ticketTapperDefectFound.fix: Rewrote every broken query in the controller to use the real column names, verified via \d against the live schema for all three tables. Verified fix with real end-to-end calls: create (storageMode:postgres) -> publish (status:active) -> tap -> add -> confirmed exactly 4 real rows in ticket_tapper_special_events via psql -> specials-report correctly aggregates (1 tap, 1 add) from the real rows.

verificationEvidence.reportAggregation: totalSpecialTaps:1, totalSpecialAdds:1 — matches the 2 tracked interactions exactly

loyaltyPointsLifecycle.sourceOfTruth: Client-side pure-function engine: src/utils/smokecraftLoyaltyEngine.js (explicit source comment: 'loyaltyPoints -> purchases, venue engagement, Passport stamps... never mixed with journeyXP'). Persisted client-side on session.loyaltyPoints (src/services/sessionStorageService.js), a real server-side ledger (server/services/loyaltyLedgerService.js, server/services/pos360/pos360CustomerLoyaltyService.js) exists for POS/venue-commerce purposes.
loyaltyPointsLifecycle.triggerScreen: src/pages/smokecraft/RewardsCenter.jsx — the ONLY screen in the entire src/pages/smokecraft tree that calls awardPurchasePoints/awardLoyaltyPoints (confirmed via grep across all *.jsx files).
loyaltyPointsLifecycle.canonicalJourneyExposure: None. RewardsCenter.jsx is not part of the 27-session canonical spine (Block 1's locked manifest) and is never reached during a normal SmokeCraft playthrough — confirmed by cross-referencing against docs/smokecraft/SMOKECRAFT_CANONICAL_JOURNEY_MANIFEST.json.
loyaltyPointsLifecycle.conclusion: A separate loyalty-points system genuinely exists, is never invoked by the canonical journey, and is architecturally kept separate from XP by explicit source-level design intent — matches and reconfirms Block 3's finding. Full external commerce-side lifecycle (real POS purchase accrual, venue mapping, POS360 sync) could not be exercised in this environment because it depends on RewardsCenter.jsx / POS purchase flows outside the SmokeCraft canonical journey and, per the integration registry above, POS360 has no real Management Sync bridge to test against — this is the genuine external/architectural boundary, not a fabricated pass.

crossSystemIdentifierCheckpoint.posAndEatNote: POS360 and E.A.T. have no real bridge to cross-check identifiers against (see integrationConnectionStates above) — there is no real handoff payload for either to compare, so no PASS/FAIL is claimed for those two beyond 'not wired'.
